title: ESSA: Explanation Iterative Supervision via Saliency-guided Data Augmentation

problem.claim: Explanation supervision guides models with human-generated explanations to improve interpretability and predictability.

gap.claim: Explanation supervision requires large-scale training data, while augmentation of medical images is challenged by scarce augmenter-training data, difficulty generating realistic images, and uncertainty about performance benefits.

contributions.claim: The ESSA framework combines explanation supervision with adversarial-trained image augmentation in a synergized iterative loop.
The framework translates annotations into sophisticated images and generates synthetic image-annotation pairs through an alternating training strategy.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on two medical-imaging datasets.
The authors report improved model predictability and explainability.

narrative_sequence.summary: Explanation supervision uses human-generated explanations to improve model interpretability and predictability.
The technique requires large-scale training data, motivating data augmentation.
Medical-image augmentation faces data scarcity, realism, and downstream-benefit challenges.
ESSA addresses these challenges with an iterative framework combining explanation supervision, saliency-guided augmentation, and alternating training.
Experiments on two medical-imaging datasets are reported to improve predictability and explainability.

source_observation.claim: The framework uses an iterative loop linking explanation supervision with synthetic image-annotation generation.

interpretation.claim: Iteratively coupling supervision signals with data generation may help align augmented data with the target learning objective.

application.claim: For explanation-guided learning with limited specialized data, consider augmentation procedures that incorporate task-relevant supervision.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy transfers beyond the reported medical-imaging setting.

unknowns: The specific datasets, metrics, baselines, and quantitative results are not provided.
The saliency-guided augmentation procedure and alternating training details are not specified.
The nature and scale of the human annotations are not specified.
